item.title: Sebi warns investors against fraudulent WhatsApp stock tip groups
item.description: The market regulator warned that unregistered entities use invitation-only WhatsApp groups, fabricated profit testimonials and overseas numbers to lure unsuspecting investors ...
item.dc:creator: Our Bureau
item.content:encoded: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) on Thursday cautioned investors against unregistered entities offering stock tips and trading calls through invitation-only WhatsApp groups, warning of misleading profit claims and fraudulent practices. The operators, often using overseas numbers, pose as market experts and encourage members to post fabricated profit testimonials to create an impression of credibility. Sebi said members are frequently invited to new groups through messages from different numbers after the original groups are suspended or banned. The regulator advised investors to avoid acting on such tips, transferring money to suggested platforms or sharing trading account details, and to deal only with Sebi-registered intermediaries.

item.title: Sunil Kumar appointed ONGC chairman for three years from December 7, 2026
item.description: The ACC has approved Sunil Kumar's appointment as ONGC chairman for a combined three-year tenure starting December 7, 2026. He will succeed Arun Singh, who took charge in 2022 ...
item.dc:creator: Our Bureau
item.content:encoded: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) has approved the appointment of Sunil Kumar, currently serving as executive director at Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC), as the next chairman of the company for three years beginning December 7, 2026. He has been appointed chairman with effect from the date he assumes charge of the post on or after December 7, until his superannuation in December 2028 and thereafter on a contract basis, for a combined tenure of three years. His name was recommended for the top post after two rounds of interviews by a search-cum-selection committee of the petroleum ministry. He will become the first chairman of the company to be elevated from the executive director rank to its top post. Kumar, 58, will replace Arun Singh, who has been the chairman and chief executive officer (CEO) of the petroleum explorer since December 2022. Kumar took charge as executive director and asset manager of ONGC's Mehsana Asset in January 2025. A petroleum engineering graduate of the Indian School of Mines, Dhanbad, he also holds a postgraduate qualification in business management, specialising in marketing and finance. The change in leadership comes at a time when ONGC, which alone accounts for 75 per cent of India's domestic crude oil and natural gas production, is facing increasing pressure to boost output and diversify into newer areas of energy transition.

item.title: Sebi allows margin relief on subsequent trades against early pay-in
item.description: Sebi has allowed margin relief on subsequent cash-market trades against accepted early pay-in of securities, easing margin requirements for clients with net sell obligations.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Markets / News / Sebi allows margin relief on subsequent trades against early pay-in

Sebi allows margin relief on subsequent trades against early pay-in Sebi has allowed margin relief on subsequent cash-market trades against accepted early pay-in of securities, easing margin requirements for clients with net sell obligations.

Sebi has allowed margin relief on subsequent cash-market trades against securities accepted under the early pay-in mechanism, subject to prescribed conditions. (Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 22 2026 | 6:57 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Market regulator Sebi on Thursday said that clearing corporations will not collect margins from trading and clearing members on clients' subsequent buy or sell positions in the cash segment, up to the value of securities for which early pay-in (EPI) has been successfully accepted.   The decision aims to provide margin relief to clients who have a net sell obligation in a settlement and have completed the EPI process through the clearing corporation.   "It is decided that where a client has a net sell obligation in a settlement, and the EPI request for the sold securities has been successfully accepted by the CC, the CC shall, on a real-time basis, not collect margin from the Trading Member (TM)/ Clearing Member (CM) on the subsequent buy/sell positions of the client, up to the amount of such accepted EPI," Sebi said in its circular.

The decision has been taken keeping in account the proposals received from the Broker ISF, recommendations of the Risk Management Review Committee (RMRC) of Sebi and internal deliberations.   Under the revised framework, clearing corporations will calculate the available EPI value on the trade date, which will be the lower of the value of securities for which EPI has been made and the value of securities sold. Also Read

Nippon Life India AMC gets Sebi nod to settle Yes Bank AT-1 bond case

NCDEX launches NDEX, FINNDEX in push to become multi-segment exchange

Jane Street appeal: SAT reserves order on plea for additional Sebi records

Best of Opinion: IDBI sale revives hopes for stalled disinvestment drive

Improved closing auction premium

When a client takes a position in the cash segment on the same day based on the EPI benefit, the clearing corporation will assess the client's available margin after reducing the eligible EPI value.   However, if a client squares off the sale position in the securities against which the EPI benefit has been availed, the EPI value will be removed. Sebi said any resulting shortfall in the client's margin will be blocked from the proprietary collateral of the trading member or clearing member.

This condition will not apply to trade-for-trade securities, as those transactions are settled on a gross basis, Sebi added. Sebi also directed trading members to ensure that their risk management systems allow clients to square off positions against which EPI benefits have been availed, or take fresh positions, only when the requisite client margins are available.

item.title: India permits 6,500 tonnes of silver imports despite weak demand
item.description: India has permitted imports of around 6,500 metric tons of silver over six months despite weak domestic demand, a move expected to ease local premiums while supporting global prices.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Economy / News / India permits 6,500 tonnes of silver imports despite weak demand

India permits 6,500 tonnes of silver imports despite weak demand India has permitted imports of around 6,500 metric tons of silver over six months despite weak domestic demand, a move expected to ease local premiums while supporting global prices.

India has permitted imports of around 6,500 metric tons of silver over the next six months, despite weak domestic demand, in a move expected to ease elevated local premiums.| Image: Bloomberg

Reuters 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 22 2026 | 6:44 PM IST

Listen to This Article

India has issued permits to import around 6,500 metric tons of silver over the next six months as the world's biggest consumer of the precious metal seeks to meet festive-season demand, four bullion dealers who received the permits told Reuters.   Higher imports by India, which relies on overseas purchases to meet more than 80% of its silver demand, could support global prices while easing hefty domestic premiums that have risen due to tight supplies.   India in mid-May restricted imports of silver in nearly all forms with immediate effect. In June, it further tightened the rules by adding silver grain and powder to the restricted category and requiring prior import authorisation.

"The government has allowed much more silver to be imported than the country is likely to need over the next six months, so this should help bring down domestic premiums," said Chirag Thakkar, chief executive of Amrapali Group Gujarat, a leading silver importer.   Silver premiums over official domestic prices fell to 45 cents per ounce on Thursday, down from up to $2.50 last week, dealers said. Also Read

Gold, silver extend losses as crude oil prices rise amid West Asia tenions

EV supply struggles to keep pace with surging demand during festive season premium

The great bull-market in India is over; prefer bonds, cash: Marc Faber

Let the people hedge premium

Climate, floods, war: Why sweets are getting costlier this festival season premium

India has been trying in recent months to curb precious metals imports to ease pressure on its foreign exchange reserves and support the rupee.   As part of those efforts, the government has raised import duties on gold and silver to 15% from 6%.

The higher import allocation for the next six months surprised the market, as domestic demand for silver jewellery and investment has remained weak amid falling prices, dealers said.   "The festive season is here, but demand is yet to pick up. Many investors have burned their fingers in the recent sharp price correction and are now staying on the sidelines," said a Mumbai-based dealer with a bullion importing bank.
